title: 363. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Surface Area of Prisms
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Total Surface Area of a Right Prism
questions.learningObjective: Identify the contributions of the lateral faces and two bases to a right prism's total surface area.
questions.question: A closed right prism has base area \(B\), base perimeter \(P\), and perpendicular height \(h\). Which expression gives its total surface area?
questions.explanation: The lateral area is the base perimeter multiplied by the prism height, \(Ph\). A closed prism also has two congruent bases, each of area \(B\). Therefore, the total surface area is \(Ph+2B\).
questions.hint: Count the two congruent bases as well as all the lateral faces.

questions.concept: Surface Area of a Rectangular Prism
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the total surface area of a rectangular prism from its three edge lengths.
questions.question: A closed rectangular prism measures \(5\text{ cm}\) by \(3\text{ cm}\) by \(2\text{ cm}\). What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: A rectangular prism has three pairs of congruent faces. Its total surface area is \(2(lw+lh+wh)\). Substituting the dimensions gives \(2(5\cdot3+5\cdot2+3\cdot2)=2(15+10+6)=62\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Find the areas of the three different rectangular faces, then account for each opposite face.

questions.concept: Surface Area of a Right Triangular Prism
questions.learningObjective: Combine the areas of two triangular bases with the lateral area of a right triangular prism.
questions.question: A closed right triangular prism has a right-triangle base with legs \(6\text{ cm}\) and \(8\text{ cm}\) and hypotenuse \(10\text{ cm}\). The length of the prism is \(12\text{ cm}\). What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: One triangular base has area \(\frac{1}{2}\cdot6\cdot8=24\text{ cm}^2\). Its perimeter is \(6+8+10=24\text{ cm}\), so the lateral area is \(24\cdot12=288\text{ cm}^2\). Adding both bases gives \(288+2\cdot24=336\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Calculate one triangular base area and the base perimeter separately before finding the total.

questions.learningObjective: Use a square base and the four lateral rectangles to calculate the surface area of a closed prism.
questions.question: A closed right prism has a square base of side length \(4\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(7\text{ cm}\). What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: The two square bases have total area \(2\cdot4^2=32\text{ cm}^2\). The four lateral rectangles have total area \(4\cdot4\cdot7=112\text{ cm}^2\). Adding both parts gives \(32+112=144\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Find the area of both square bases, not just one, before adding the side faces.

questions.concept: Triangular Base Area and Lateral Area
questions.learningObjective: Use a supplied triangle altitude and side lengths to find the total surface area of a triangular prism.
questions.question: The base of a closed right triangular prism is an isosceles triangle with sides \(5\text{ cm}\), \(5\text{ cm}\), and \(6\text{ cm}\). The altitude to the \(6\text{ cm}\) side is \(4\text{ cm}\). The prism is \(9\text{ cm}\) long. What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: The triangular base area is \(\frac{1}{2}\cdot6\cdot4=12\text{ cm}^2\), and its perimeter is \(5+5+6=16\text{ cm}\). The lateral area is \(16\cdot9=144\text{ cm}^2\). Add the two triangular bases: \(144+2\cdot12=168\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: The triangle altitude determines each base area, while the three side lengths determine the lateral area.

questions.concept: Recovering Prism Height from Surface Area
questions.learningObjective: Determine a rectangular prism's unknown height from its total surface area and base dimensions.
questions.question: A closed right rectangular prism has a base measuring \(6\text{ cm}\) by \(4\text{ cm}\) and total surface area \(208\text{ cm}^2\). What is the perpendicular height of the prism?
questions.explanation: If the height is \(h\), the two bases contribute \(2(6\cdot4)=48\text{ cm}^2\), and the lateral area is \(2(6+4)h=20h\). Hence \(48+20h=208\), so \(20h=160\) and \(h=8\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Subtract the areas of the two bases first, then divide the remaining area by the base perimeter.

questions.concept: Surface Area of a Trapezoidal Prism
questions.learningObjective: Combine trapezoid area and perimeter to determine the total surface area of a right prism.
questions.question: A closed right prism has an isosceles trapezoid as its base. The parallel sides are \(6\text{ cm}\) and \(14\text{ cm}\), the other two sides are each \(5\text{ cm}\), and the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides is \(3\text{ cm}\). The prism is \(8\text{ cm}\) long. What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: One trapezoidal base has area \(\frac{1}{2}(6+14)\cdot3=30\text{ cm}^2\). Its perimeter is \(6+14+5+5=30\text{ cm}\), giving lateral area \(30\cdot8=240\text{ cm}^2\). The total is \(240+2\cdot30=300\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Use the parallel sides and their perpendicular distance for the base area; use all four sides for the perimeter.

questions.concept: Surface Area of an Open-Top Rectangular Prism
questions.learningObjective: Select only the present faces when calculating the surface area of an open-top prism-shaped container.
questions.question: An open-top rectangular container has internal length \(8\text{ cm}\), width \(5\text{ cm}\), and height \(4\text{ cm}\). Ignoring wall thickness, what area of material is needed for its bottom and four side faces?
questions.explanation: The bottom contributes \(8\cdot5=40\text{ cm}^2\). The two longer sides contribute \(2(8\cdot4)=64\text{ cm}^2\), and the two shorter sides contribute \(2(5\cdot4)=40\text{ cm}^2\). The open top is excluded, so \(40+64+40=144\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: A container with no top has only five faces to include.

questions.concept: Comparing Surface Areas at Equal Volume
questions.learningObjective: Compare the total surface areas of two rectangular prisms with equal volumes but different edge lengths.
questions.question: Two closed rectangular prisms both have volume \(144\text{ cm}^3\). Prism X measures \(4\text{ cm}\) by \(4\text{ cm}\) by \(9\text{ cm}\); Prism Y measures \(3\text{ cm}\) by \(6\text{ cm}\) by \(8\text{ cm}\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Prism X has \(4\text{ cm}^2\) less surface area than Prism Y.

options.label: B
options.text: Prism Y has \(4\text{ cm}^2\) less surface area than Prism X.

questions.explanation: For Prism X, the surface area is \(2(4\cdot4+4\cdot9+4\cdot9)=176\text{ cm}^2\). For Prism Y, it is \(2(3\cdot6+3\cdot8+6\cdot8)=180\text{ cm}^2\). Thus Prism X has \(180-176=4\text{ cm}^2\) less surface area, even though their volumes are equal.
questions.hint: Calculate each surface area independently; equal volume does not guarantee equal surface area.

questions.concept: Surface Area Change After Cutting a Prism
questions.learningObjective: Determine the combined surface area after a rectangular prism is split into two smaller prisms.
questions.question: A closed rectangular prism measures \(12\text{ cm}\) by \(8\text{ cm}\) by \(5\text{ cm}\). It is cut into two congruent rectangular prisms by a plane perpendicular to the \(12\text{ cm}\) edge. After the cut, what is the sum of the total surface areas of the two smaller prisms?
questions.explanation: The original prism has surface area \(2(12\cdot8+12\cdot5+8\cdot5)=392\text{ cm}^2\). Cutting perpendicular to the \(12\text{ cm}\) edge exposes two new rectangular faces, each of area \(8\cdot5=40\text{ cm}^2\). Thus the two smaller prisms have combined surface area \(392+2\cdot40=472\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: A cut leaves the original outer faces and creates one new exposed face on each smaller prism.
